name: Vitamin B12
summary: Vitamin B12, also known as cobalamin, is a B vitamin and essential human micronutrient. Vitamin B12 is needed in the metabolism of every cell in the body, and has many vital functions, particularly, DNA synthesis. It plays an essential role in the nervous system by supporting myelin synthesis and for the maturation of red blood cells in the bone marrow.

pharmacology.text: A related cause is reduced stomach acid production with age or from long-term use of proton-pump inhibitors, H2 blockers, or other antacids, and interaction with metformin.

body.says: Readily absorbed in the distal half of the ileum.
Approximately 6 days; (400 days in the liver).

uses.text: Supplements are commonly taken orally but may be administered via intramuscular injection to treat deficiencies.
uses.routes: By mouth, sublingual, intravenous (IV), intramuscular (IM), intranasal
